patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with sudden-onset symptoms of vertigo.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Doctor, I’m a 59-year-old man. About three minutes ago, I suddenly felt the room spinning when I was going to bed, and I had a few episodes of nausea and vomiting, but now I feel back to my baseline.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any involuntary movements recently—like twitching, jerking, shaking, or sudden uncontrollable movements that you can’t stop? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t had any twitching, jerking, shaking, or sudden uncontrollable movements.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a **lump in your right breast that doesn’t hurt** and feels like it **moves or shifts** when you touch it? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t noticed any lump in my right breast, and nothing has been shifting or moving when I touch it.”

turns.doctor_question: When you press or gently tap around your belly button area, does it feel tender or painful? (yes/no)
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—it doesn’t feel tender or painful when you press or gently tap around my belly button.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a lump or mass in your **right breast** (for example, a new or growing area you can feel)?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t noticed any lump or mass in my right breast, and nothing new has been growing or changing there.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that the lenses in **both eyes** look **cloudy or hazy**, like you’re seeing through a fog or film? (Yes/No)
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—my vision doesn’t look cloudy or hazy in either eye.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any **unintentional weight loss** recently—meaning you’ve lost weight without trying (for example, over the past few months)?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t had any unintentional weight loss recently; my weight has been pretty stable.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a **lump or mass in your right breast that doesn’t hurt** (painless), even if it’s small?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t noticed any lump or mass in my right breast, and nothing painless or small that I can feel.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been pregnant recently, or is there any chance you could be pregnant right now?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I’m not pregnant—at all, and I don’t have any chance of being pregnant.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a breast lump or swelling that seems to move or shift when you touch it, rather than staying fixed in one spot?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t noticed any breast lump or swelling that moves or shifts when I touch it; there isn’t anything I can feel like that.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself avoiding using your right knee because it hurts? (yes/no)
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I’m not avoiding using my right knee because it hurts; I don’t have any right knee pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that you’ve been walking more slowly than usual lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t been walking more slowly than usual; my walking feels the same as always.”

turns.doctor_question: I’m sorry you’re dealing with this. To check for **lower abdominal discomfort**: **have you been feeling any pain, cramping, or discomfort in the lower part of your belly** (below your belly button)?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t had any pain, cramping, or discomfort in the lower part of my belly below my belly button.”
